Metadata.appDescription: See every night of your PAP therapy in detail.
Metadata.therapyDescription: Your nightly PAP therapy data, night after night.

Landing.seoDescription: Review your PAP therapy data on the web from any device, with nightly detail, AHI, leak, pressure and long-term trends in one history.
Landing.heroTitle: See every night in full detail.
Landing.heroBody: PapSee turns your PAP therapy data into an account-linked, night-by-night history. Follow the detail and changes over time from your phone, tablet or computer.
Landing.whyTitle: Your therapy history should not be tied to one computer or an SD card.
Landing.whyBody: Add your data to your account once. PapSee brings your nights together in a modern web interface, ready whenever you sign in on your phone, tablet or computer.
Landing.accessBody: Sign in from a browser without installing software. See the same nightly detail on your phone, tablet or computer.
Landing.cardFreeTitle: Leave the SD card at home
Landing.cardFreeBody: After an import, your nights stay with your account. You do not need the card or your PAP device beside you to review them.
Landing.sharingBody: Create a link that lets doctors review your nights without needing an account, or export your data on the fly without carrying an SD card.
Landing.securityBody: Your health data is stored securely.
Landing.signalEyebrow: One night, without the blind spots
Landing.signalTitle: The detail is there when you need it.
Landing.signalBody: Open a night and read flow, mask pressure and leak on the same timeline. Events stay aligned across every signal, so the surrounding context remains visible.
Landing.signalPreviewLabel: Signals from the example patient night
Landing.signalPreviewDescription: A five-minute window from the example night, with one recorded event shown across every signal.
Landing.trendTitle: One night is a data point. The pattern appears over time.
Landing.trendBody: Compare recent nights with the period before them and follow AHI, usage, leak and pressure together. See whether a change belongs to one night or continues across the weeks.
Landing.trendPreviewDescription: Each bar is one night from the example patient.
Landing.trendChartLabel: AHI across 30 nights for the example patient
Landing.howTitle: From one night to the bigger picture.
Landing.stepBringBody: Add what your compatible PAP device recorded to the history on your account.
Landing.stepReadBody: Read the summary first, then move into signals, events, sessions and settings.
Landing.stepReturnBody: Follow your therapy across weeks and months from any device where you sign in.
Landing.coverageTitle: Honest about what it can read.
Landing.coverageBody: PapSee reads ResMed cards today. It is verified against a real AirSense 11 card, and the AirSense 10, AirCurve and S9 formats are implemented and tested against synthetic cards. Other brands are recognised by name so an unreadable card is never mistaken for an empty night.
Landing.sourceTitle: Read the code, or self host it on your own computer.
Landing.sourceBody: PapSee is free software under the AGPL. You can read exactly what happens to a night you import, report a number that looks wrong, or self host the whole thing so your therapy data never leaves a computer you control.
Landing.closingTitle: Turn your nights into a history you can read.
Landing.closingBody: Keep the detail your PAP device recorded in one place and follow what changes over time.
Landing.disclaimer: PapSee shows what your PAP device recorded. It does not provide a diagnosis or medical advice.
Landing.nightsDescription: Hours slept and AHI, newest first.

Terms.ahiBody: Apnea-hypopnea index: how many apneas and hypopneas your device counted per hour of use. Your device scores these from airflow alone. A sleep study also watches brain activity, so its AHI and this one are not the same number.
Terms.severityBody: The usual clinical reference scale for a diagnostic sleep study: under 5 is the normal range, 5 to under 15 mild, 15 to under 30 moderate, 30 and above severe. Shown here so the number has something to be read against. This is therapy data, not a diagnosis.
Terms.oaiBody: Obstructive apnea index: obstructive apneas per hour of use.
Terms.caiBody: Clear airway index: apneas per hour of use where your device saw no effort to breathe.
Terms.hiBody: Hypopnea index: hypopneas per hour of use.
Terms.reraBody: Respiratory effort related arousal: a run of breaths where effort rises or airflow flattens, ending in a stir, without going far enough to be an apnea or a hypopnea. RERAs are counted separately and are not part of the AHI.
Terms.obstructiveApneaBody: Airflow all but stops for at least ten seconds while you keep trying to breathe. The airway itself is blocked.
Terms.clearAirwayBody: Airflow all but stops for at least ten seconds and your device sees no attempt to breathe. Your device calls these Clear Airway because it judges the airway open; a sleep study would call them central apneas.
Terms.hypopneaBody: Airflow drops by roughly a third or more for at least ten seconds without stopping. A partial narrowing rather than a blockage.
Terms.periodicBreathingBody: A stretch where breathing swells and fades in a repeating cycle. Your device reports the minutes it saw, not a count.
Terms.usageBody: How long the mask was actually on and delivering therapy over the night, added up across every time you put it on.
Terms.eprBody: Expiratory pressure relief: your device holds the treatment pressure while you breathe in and drops it by the set level while you breathe out, which makes exhaling feel less like pushing. Levels run 1 to 3 cmH2O.
Terms.rampBody: A gentler start. Therapy begins below your treatment pressure and rises to it, either over a set number of minutes or once your device detects that you have fallen asleep.
Terms.maskPressureBody: The pressure your device delivered at the mask, moment by moment, in cmH2O. It moves with every breath when EPR is on.
Terms.therapyPressureBody: The pressure your device decided to deliver, before EPR trims the exhale. On AutoSet it moves through the night as your device reads your breathing.
Terms.expiratoryPressureBody: The pressure left while you breathe out, once EPR has taken its level off the therapy pressure. With EPR off it sits on top of the therapy pressure.
Terms.targetEpapBody: The pressure your device was aiming to hold while you breathe out.
Terms.leakBody: Air escaping somewhere other than through you, in litres per minute. Your device reports it after subtracting the deliberate leak your mask vents by design.
Terms.largeLeakBody: Leak high enough that your device may no longer be seeing your breathing clearly, so the events it counts during that stretch are less reliable. Your device does not set a threshold itself; the line drawn here is a common reference point.
Terms.flowBody: Air moving in and out through the mask, breath by breath. Above the line is breathing in, below it is breathing out. This is the trace every scored event is read from.
Terms.flowLimitationBody: How flattened the shape of each breath in is, compared with an unobstructed breath. Rising flow limitation is a sign of the airway narrowing before it closes far enough to be scored.
Terms.tidalVolumeBody: The volume of air in one breath, in millilitres.
Terms.minuteVentilationBody: How much air you moved per minute: tidal volume multiplied by respiratory rate.
Terms.snoreBody: A measure of the vibration your device picked up in the airflow. It is your device's own scale, not decibels.
Terms.oxygenSaturationBody: The share of your haemoglobin carrying oxygen, as a percentage. Only recorded if an oximeter was attached to your device.
Terms.pulseBody: Heartbeats per minute, from an attached oximeter.
Terms.medianBody: The middle reading of the night: half the night was above it, half below. Less easily pulled about by a few extreme moments than an average.
Terms.percentile95Body: The reading that 95 per cent of the night stayed below. A way of seeing the high end without letting a single spike stand for the night.
Terms.timeAtPressureBody: How many minutes of the night were spent at each pressure. A wide spread means your device moved around a lot; a narrow peak means it settled and stayed there.
Terms.eprFullTimeBody: Full Time means the device eased the pressure on every exhale, all night. The other setting, Ramp Only, eases it just while the pressure is still rising at the start.
